controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of security, compliance and resilience governance controls.

controls.name: Publishing Security, Compliance & Resilience Documentation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish, maintain and disseminate policies, standards and procedures necessary for secure, compliant and resilient capabilities.

controls.name: Periodic Review & Update of Security, Compliance & Resilience Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to review the Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP), including policies, standards and procedures, at planned intervals or if significant changes occur to ensure their continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

controls.name: Assigned Security, Compliance & Resilience Responsibilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to assign one or more qualified individuals with the mission and resources to centrally-manage, coordinate, develop, implement and maintain an enterprise-wide Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP).

controls.name: Measures of Performance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, report and monitor Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) measures of performance.

controls.name: Contacts With Authorities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document appropriate contacts with relevant law enforcement and regulatory bodies.

controls.name: Contacts With Groups & Associations
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to establish contact with selected groups and associations within the security, compliance and resilience communities to: 
(1) Facilitate ongoing cybersecurity and data protection education and training for organizational personnel;
(2) Maintain currency with recommended cybersecurity and data protection practices, techniques and technologies; and
(3) Share current cybersecurity and/or data protection-related information including threats, vulnerabilities and incidents.

controls.name: Defining Business Context & Mission
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define the context of its business model and document the organization's mission.

controls.name: Define Control Objectives
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish control objectives as the basis for the selection, implementation and management of the organization's internal security, compliance and resilience control system.

controls.name: Data Governance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate data governance to oversee the organization's policies, standards and procedures so that sensitive/regulated data is effectively managed and maintained in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Purpose Validation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor mission/business-critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to ensure those resources are being used consistent with their intended purpose.

controls.name: Forced Technology Transfer (FTT)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to avoid and/or constrain the forced exfiltration of sensitive/regulated information (e.g., Intellectual Property (IP)) to the host government for purposes of market access or market management practices.

controls.name: State-Sponsored Espionage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to constrain the host government's ability to leverage the organization's Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for economic or political espionage and/or cyberwarfare activities.

controls.name: Business As Usual (BAU) Security, Compliance & Resilience Practices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to incorporate security, compliance and resilience principles into Business As Usual (BAU) practices through executive leadership involvement.

controls.name: Operationalizing Security, Compliance & Resilience Capabilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to compel data and/or process owners to operationalize security, compliance and resilience practices for each Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) under their control.

controls.name: Materiality Determination
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define materiality threshold criteria capable of designating an incident as material.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Status Reporting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to submit status reporting of the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience program to applicable statutory and/or regulatory authorities, as required.

controls.name: Quality Management System (QMS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern a Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure security, compliance and resilience processes conform with applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Assurance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define the basis for confidence that implemented practices conform to applicable security, compliance and resilience controls, where the control implementation performs as intended.

controls.name: Mergers, Acquisitions & Divestitures (MA&D)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define standardized practices to conduct Mergers, Acquisitions and Divestiture (MA&D) activities.

controls.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Autonomous Technologies Governance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure policies, processes, procedures and practices related to the mapping, measuring and managing of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks are in place, transparent and implemented effectively.

controls.name: Situational Awareness of AI & Autonomous Technologies
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop and maintain an inventory of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) (internal and third-party).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Context Definition
AI & Autonomous Technologies Business Case
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to benchmark capabilities, targeted usage, goals and expected benefits and costs of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure personnel and external stakeholders are provided with position-specific risk management training for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Fairness & Bias
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) from unfairly identifying, profiling and/or statistically singling out a segmented population defined by race, religion, gender identity, national origin, religion, disability or any other politically-charged identifier.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Management Decisions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to leverage decision makers from a diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise and backgrounds for mapping, measuring and managing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks.

controls.name: Assigned Responsibilities for AI & Autonomous Technologies
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for:
(1) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) configurations; and
(2) Oversight of AAT systems.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Profiling
Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV) practices to enable Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related security, resilience and compliance-related conformity testing throughout the lifecycle of the AAT.

controls.name: Robust Stakeholder Engagement for AI & Autonomous Technologies
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to compel ongoing engagement with relevant Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) stakeholders to encourage feedback about positive, negative and unanticipated impacts.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Intellectual Property Infringement Protections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent third-party Intellectual Property (IP) rights infringement by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Stakeholder Diversity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) stakeholder competencies, skills and capacities incorporate demographic diversity, broad domain and user experience expertise.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Requirements Definitions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to take socio-technical implications into account to address risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Viability Decisions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define the criteria as to whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) achieved intended purposes and stated objectives to determine whether its development or deployment should proceed.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Production Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor the functionality and behavior of the deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Harm Prevention
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively prevent harm by regularly identifying and tracking existing, unanticipated and emergent Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Tracking Approaches
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to track Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Conformity
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to ensure deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) conform to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, based on:
(1) Defined use cases;
(2) Geographic markets; and
(3) Use of Intellectual Property (IP).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Development Practices
controls.description:
Measures exist to ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are designed and developed to:
(1) Achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity; 
(2) Perform consistently in those respects throughout the AAT system's lifecycle; and
(3) Be effectively overseen by competent individuals.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Registration
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a current registration for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) with the appropriate governing body, as required by statutory or regulatory requirements.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Deployment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) includes appropriate technical and organizational measures so that AAT are used in accordance with the AAT developer-provided instructions for use.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Marking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to mark output from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) in a machine-readable format so it is detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

controls.name: Real World Testing of AI & Autonomous Technologies
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to obtain consent from the subjects of testing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT):
(1) Prior to their participation in such testing; and
(2) After they have been provided with clear and concise information regarding the testing.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies System Value Chain
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to document the sequence of events and relevant stakeholders involved in creating and deploying Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Testing Techniques
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop and implement fact-checking techniques to verify the accuracy and veracity of information generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT).

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Filtering
AI Model Resilience
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure AI models are designed with resilience capabilities that are sufficient to withstand reasonable threats.

controls.name: AI Agent Governance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure AI agents are designed, developed and deployed to securely operate under human oversight.

controls.name: Agentic Output Traceability & Repudiation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure AI agent actions offer non-repudiation and enable forensic examination to determine accountability.

controls.name: Human-in-the-Loop Workload & Manipulation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent cognitive overload or decision fatigue for humans-in-the-loop (HITL) through risk-based prioritization.

controls.name: Robotic Process Automation (RPA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Robotic Process Automation (RPA) to improve efficiency, accuracy and speed for high-volume, repetitive and rules-based business processes.

controls.name: Asset Governance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate an IT Asset Management (ITAM) program to implement and manage asset management controls.

controls.name: Asset Inventories
Asset Ownership Assignment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure asset ownership responsibilities are assigned, tracked and managed at a team, individual, or responsible organization level to establish a common understanding of requirements for asset protection.

controls.name: Network Diagrams & Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to maintain network architecture diagrams that: 
(1) Contain sufficient detail to assess the security of the network's architecture;
(2) Reflect the current architecture of the network environment; and
(3) Document all sensitive/regulated data flows.

controls.name: Security of Assets & Media
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain strict control over the internal or external distribution of any kind of sensitive/regulated media.

controls.name: Unattended End-User Equipment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement enhanced protection measures for unattended technology assets to protect against tampering and unauthorized access.

controls.name: Kiosks & Point of Interaction (PoI) Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to appropriately protect devices that capture sensitive/regulated data via direct physical interaction from tampering and substitution.

controls.name: Physical Tampering Detection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically inspect systems and system components for Indicators of Compromise (IoC).

controls.name: Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy or repurpose system components using organization-defined techniques and methods to prevent information being recovered from these components.

controls.name: Return of Assets
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that employees and third-party users return all organizational assets in their possession upon termination of employment, contract or agreement.

controls.name: Removal of Assets
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to authorize, control and track technology assets entering and exiting organizational facilities.

controls.name: Use of Personal Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the possession and/or use of personally-owned Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within organization-controlled facilities.

controls.name: Use of Third-Party Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to reduce the risk associated with third-party assets that are attached to the network from harming organizational assets or exfiltrating organizational data.

controls.name: Usage Parameters
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor and enforce usage parameters that limit the potential damage caused from the unauthorized or unintentional alteration of system parameters.

controls.name: Logical Tampering Protection
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to assess the integrity of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to detect evidence of tampering, where:
(1)	Logical assessments evaluate the integrity of critical components (e.g., configuration settings); and
(2)	Physical assessments evaluate assets for evidence of unauthorized access and/or modifications.

controls.name: Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Usage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) program to reduce risk associated with personally-owned devices in the workplace.

controls.name: Prohibited Equipment & Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) sanctions that require the removal and prohibition of certain Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are designated as supply chain threats by a statutory or regulatory body.

controls.name: Roots of Trust Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provision and protect the confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of product supplier keys and data that can be used as a “roots of trust” basis for integrity verification.

controls.name: Telecommunications Equipment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance for telecommunication equipment to prevent potential damage or unauthorized modification and to prevent potential eavesdropping.

controls.name: Video Teleconference (VTC) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement secure Video Teleconference (VTC) capabilities on endpoint devices and in designated conference rooms, to prevent potential eavesdropping.

controls.name: Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement secure Internet Protocol Telephony (IPT) that logically or physically separates Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) traffic from data networks.

controls.name: Microphones & Web Cameras
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure assets to prohibit the use of endpoint-based microphones and web cameras in secure areas or where sensitive/regulated information is discussed.

controls.name: Multi-Function Devices (MFD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely configure Multi-Function Devices (MFD) according to industry-recognized secure practices for the type of device.

controls.name: Travel-Only Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to issue personnel travelling overseas with temporary, loaner or "travel-only" end user technology (e.g., laptops and mobile devices) when travelling to authoritarian countries with a higher-than average risk for Intellectual Property (IP) theft or espionage against individuals and private companies.

controls.name: Re-Imaging Devices After Travel
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to re-image end user technology (e.g., laptops and mobile devices) when returning from overseas travel to an authoritarian country with a higher-than average risk for Intellectual Property (IP) theft or espionage against individuals and private companies.

controls.name: System Administrative Processes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, implement and govern system administration processes, with corresponding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), for operating and maintaining Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Jump Server
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct remote system administrative functions via a "jump box" or "jump server" that is located in a separate network zone to user workstations.

controls.name: Database Administrative Processes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, implement and govern database management processes, with corresponding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), for operating and maintaining databases.

controls.name: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely govern Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) deployments to ensure RFID is used safely and securely to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data and prevent the compromise of secure spaces.

controls.name: Decommissioning
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are properly decommissioned so that data is properly transitioned to new systems or archived in accordance with applicable organizational standards, as well as statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Asset Categorization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to categorize Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Automated Network Asset Discovery
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to automate network asset discovery through Software Defined Networking (SDN), or similar technologies, that analyzes network traffic to:
(1) Identify;
(2) Document; and 
(3) Track devices.

controls.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of contingency planning controls to help ensure resilient Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) (e.g., Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) or Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) playbooks).

controls.name: Identify Critical Assets
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document the critical Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that support essential missions and business functions.

controls.name: Contingency Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to adequately train contingency personnel and applicable stakeholders in their contingency roles and responsibilities.

controls.name: Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct tests and/or exercises to evaluate the contingency plan's effectiveness and the organization's readiness to execute the plan.

controls.name: Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and "lessons learned" activity every time the contingency plan is activated.

controls.name: Ongoing Contingency Planning
Alternative Security Measures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement alternative or compensating controls to satisfy security functions when the primary means of implementing the security function is unavailable or compromised.

controls.name: Alternate Storage Site
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish an alternate storage site that includes both the assets and necessary agreements to permit the storage and recovery of system backup information.

controls.name: Alternate Processing Site
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish an alternate processing site that provides security measures equivalent to that of the primary site.

controls.name: Telecommunications Services Availability
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to reduce the likelihood of a single point of failure with primary telecommunications services.

controls.name: Data Backups
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).

controls.name: Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) Recovery & Reconstitution
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure the secure recovery and reconstitution of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to a known state after a disruption, compromise or failure.

controls.name: Backup & Restoration Hardware Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect backup and restoration hardware and software.

controls.name: Isolated Recovery Environment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize an isolated, non-production environment to perform data backup and recovery operations through offline, cloud or off-site capabilities.

controls.name: Reserve Hardware
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to purchase and maintain a sufficient reserve of spare hardware to ensure essential missions and business functions can be maintained in the event of a supply chain disruption.

controls.name: AI & Autonomous Technologies Incidents
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to handle failures or incidents with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) deemed to be high-risk.

controls.name: Capacity & Performance Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of capacity management controls to ensure optimal system performance to meet expected and anticipated future capacity requirements.

controls.name: Resource Priority
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control resource utilization of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are susceptible to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to limit and prioritize the use of resources.

controls.name: Capacity Planning
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct capacity planning so that necessary capacity for information processing, telecommunications and environmental support will exist during contingency operations.

controls.name: Performance Monitoring
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to centrally-monitor and alert on the operating state and health status of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Elastic Expansion
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to automatically scale the resources available for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), as demand conditions change.

controls.name: Regional Delivery
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to support operations that are geographically dispersed via regional delivery of technological Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Change Management Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of a change management program.

controls.name: Configuration Change Control
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern the technical configuration change control processes.

controls.name: Security Impact Analysis for Changes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to analyze proposed changes for potential security impacts, prior to the implementation of the change.

controls.name: Access Restriction For Change
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce configuration restrictions in an effort to restrict the ability of users to conduct unauthorized changes.

controls.name: Stakeholder Notification of Changes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure stakeholders are made aware of and understand the impact of proposed changes.

controls.name: Control Functionality Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to verify the functionality of security, compliance and resilience controls following implemented changes to ensure applicable controls operate as designed.

controls.name: Emergency Changes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern change management procedures for "emergency" changes.

controls.name: Dual Approval For High-Impact Environments
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to require dual approval for any changes that might result in a serious incident that could adversely impact:
(1) Business processes; and/or
(2) Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.name: Cloud Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of cloud management controls to ensure cloud instances are secure and in-line with industry practices.

controls.name: Cloud Security Architecture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure the cloud security architecture supports the organization's technology strategy to securely design, configure and maintain cloud employments.

controls.name: Cloud Infrastructure Security Subnet
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to host security-specific technologies in a dedicated subnet.

controls.name: Application Programming Interface (API) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure support for secure interoperability between components with Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).

controls.name: Virtual Machine Images
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure the integrity of virtual machine images at all times.

controls.name: Multi-Tenant Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure multi-tenant owned or managed assets (physical and virtual) are designed and governed such that provider and customer (tenant) user access is appropriately segmented from other tenant users.

controls.name: Data Handling & Portability
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure cloud providers use secure protocols for the import, export and management of data in cloud-based Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Standardized Virtualization Formats
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure interoperability by requiring cloud providers to use industry-recognized formats and provide documentation of custom changes for review.

controls.name: Geolocation Requirements for Processing, Storage and Service Locations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control the location of cloud processing/storage based on business requirements that includes statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Sensitive Data In Public Cloud Providers
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit and manage the storage of sensitive/regulated data in public cloud providers.

controls.name: Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), or similar technology, to provide boundary protection and monitoring functions that both provide access to the cloud and protect the organization from misuse of cloud resources.

controls.name: Side Channel Attack Prevention
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent "side channel attacks" when using a Content Delivery Network (CDN) by restricting access to the origin server's IP address to the CDN and an authorized management network.

controls.name: Hosted Assets, Applications & Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to specify applicable security, compliance and resilience that must be implemented on external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), consistent with the contractual obligations established with the External Service Providers (ESP) owning, operating and/or maintaining external TAAS.

controls.name: Prohibition On Unverified Hosted Assets, Applications & Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prohibit access to, or usage of, hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) until applicable security, compliance and/or resilience control implementation is verified.

controls.name: Software Defined Storage (SDS)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to utilize Software Defined Storage (SDS) to scale access management permissions to Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls Oversight
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide a security, compliance and resilience controls oversight function that reports to the organization's executive leadership.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Assessments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to regularly review processes and documented procedures to ensure conformity with the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements.

controls.name: Audit Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to thoughtfully plan audits by including input from operational risk and compliance partners to minimize the impact of audit-related activities on business operations.

controls.name: Legal Assessment of Investigative Inquires
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to determine whether a government agency has an applicable and valid legal basis to request data from the organization and what further steps need to be taken, if necessary.

controls.name: Government Surveillance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to constrain the host government from having unrestricted and non-monitored access to the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that could potentially violate other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Grievances
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern the intake and analysis of grievances related to the organization's cybersecurity and/or data protection practices.

controls.name: Localized Representation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to appoint localized representation with a physical presence in localities, as required by applicable laws and/or regulations.

controls.name: Control Reciprocity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define instances of control reciprocity within assessment boundaries.

controls.name: Control Inheritance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define instances of control inheritance within assessment boundaries.

controls.name: Dual Use Technology
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to govern technologies and/or data that have potential:
(1) "Dual-use” capabilities for civil and military;
(2) Use by terrorists; and/or 
(3) Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) applications.

controls.name: Statement of Applicability (SOA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to produce a Statement of Applicability (SOA), or similar document, for compliance-related scoping activities.

controls.name: Work Products
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to produce work products (e.g., process artifacts) that demonstrate the ability to comply with applicable requirements.

controls.name: Configuration Management Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of configuration management controls.

controls.name: Secure Baseline Configurations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, document and maintain secure baseline configurations for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are consistent with industry-accepted system hardening standards.

controls.name: Least Functionality
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure systems to provide only essential capabilities by specifically prohibiting or restricting the use of ports, protocols, and/or services.

controls.name: Software Usage Restrictions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce software usage restrictions to comply with applicable contract agreements and copyright laws.

controls.name: User-Installed Software
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the ability of non-privileged users to install unauthorized software.

controls.name: Configuration Enforcement
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to monitor, enforce and report on configurations for endpoint devices.

controls.name: Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP), or similar technology, to automatically and securely configure devices upon being added to a network.

controls.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Access Enforcement
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to restrict access to sensitive/regulated data.

controls.name: Continuous Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls.

controls.name: Centralized Collection of Security Event Logs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support the centralized collection of security-related event logs.

controls.name: Content of Event Logs
Event Log Storage Capacity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allocate and proactively manage sufficient event log storage capacity to reduce the likelihood of such capacity being exceeded.

controls.name: Response To Event Log Processing Failures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to alert appropriate personnel in the event of a log processing failure and take actions to remedy the disruption.

controls.name: Monitoring Reporting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide an event log report generation capability to aid in detecting and assessing anomalous activities.

controls.name: Time Stamps
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to use an authoritative time source to generate time stamps for event logs.

controls.name: Protection of Event Logs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect event logs and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion.

controls.name: Non-Repudiation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a non-repudiation capability to protect against an individual falsely denying having performed a particular action.

controls.name: Event Log Retention
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to retain event logs for a time period consistent with records retention requirements to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of security incidents and to meet statutory, regulatory and contractual retention requirements.

controls.name: Monitoring For Information Disclosure
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of non-public information.

controls.name: Session Audit
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide session audit capabilities that can: 
(1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
(2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time.

controls.name: Alternate Event Logging Capability
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide an alternate event logging capability in the event of a failure in primary audit capability.

controls.name: Cross-Organizational Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate sanitized event logs among external organizations to identify anomalous events when event logs are shared across organizational boundaries, without giving away sensitive or critical business data.

controls.name: Covert Channel Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct covert channel analysis to identify aspects of communications that are potential avenues for covert channels.

controls.name: Anomalous Behavior
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and/or User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solutions to detect and respond to anomalous behavior that could indicate account compromise or other malicious activities.

controls.name: Event Log Analysis & Triage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure event log reviews include analysis and triage practices that integrate with the organization's established incident response processes.

controls.name: File Activity Monitoring (FAM)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to monitor sensitive/regulated data in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and data repositories.

controls.name: Write Once Read Many (WORM) Event Log Generation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to produce event logs on hardware-enforced, write-once media (e.g., Write Once Read Many (WORM) technologies).

controls.name: Use of Cryptographic Controls
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of cryptographic protections controls using known public standards and trusted cryptographic technologies.

controls.name: Automated Authentication Through Cryptographic Modules
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to enable systems to authenticate to a cryptographic module.

controls.name: Transmission Confidentiality
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality of data being transmitted.

controls.name: Transmission Integrity
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the integrity of data being transmitted.

controls.name: Encrypting Data At Rest
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to prevent unauthorized disclosure of data at rest.

controls.name: Non-Console Administrative Access
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality and integrity of non-console administrative access.

controls.name: Wireless Access Authentication & Encryption
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality and integrity of wireless networking technologies by implementing authentication and strong encryption.

controls.name: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely implement an internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) infrastructure or obtain PKI services from a reputable PKI service provider.

controls.name: Cryptographic Key Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate cryptographic key management controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of keys.

controls.name: Transmission of Cybersecurity & Data Protection Attributes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to associate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) security attributes with information exchanged between TAAS.

controls.name: Certificate Authorities
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to enable the use of organization-defined Certificate Authorities (CAs) to facilitate the establishment of protected sessions.

controls.name: Certificate Monitoring
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to discover when new certificates are issued for organization-controlled domains.

controls.name: Cryptographic Hash
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize hash algorithms to generate a hash value that can be used to validate the integrity of data and/or software.

controls.name: Data Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of data protection controls.

controls.name: Data & Asset Classification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure data and assets are categorized in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.

controls.name: Media Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control and restrict access to digital and non-digital media to authorized individuals.

controls.name: Media Marking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to mark media in accordance with data protection requirements so that personnel are alerted to distribution limitations, handling caveats and applicable security requirements.

controls.name: Cybersecurity & Data Protection Attributes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to bind cybersecurity and data protection attributes to information as it is stored, transmitted and processed.

controls.name: Media Storage
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to: 
(1) Physically control and securely store digital and non-digital media within controlled areas using organization-defined security measures; and
(2) Protect system media until the media are destroyed or sanitized using approved equipment, techniques and procedures.

controls.name: Media Transportation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect and control digital and non-digital media during transport outside of controlled areas using appropriate security measures.

controls.name: Physical Media Disposal
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of media when it is no longer required, using formal procedures.

controls.name: System Media Sanitization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to sanitize system media with the strength and integrity commensurate with the classification or sensitivity of the information prior to disposal, release out of organizational control or release for reuse.

controls.name: Media Use
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the use of types of digital media on systems or system components.

controls.name: Data Reclassification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to reclassify data, including associated Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), commensurate with the security category and/or classification level of the information.

controls.name: Removable Media Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict removable media in accordance with data handling and acceptable usage parameters.

controls.name: Use of External Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern how external parties, including Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), are used to securely store, process and transmit data.

controls.name: Information Sharing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a process to assist users in making information sharing decisions to ensure data is appropriately protected.

controls.name: Publicly Accessible Content
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control publicly-accessible content.

controls.name: Data Mining Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect data storage objects against unauthorized data mining and data harvesting techniques.

controls.name: Ad-Hoc Transfers
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to secure ad-hoc exchanges of large digital files with internal or external parties.

controls.name: Media & Data Retention
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to retain media and data in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Geographic Location of Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to inventory, document and maintain data flows for data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within a service's geographically distributed applications (physical and virtual), infrastructure, systems components and/or shared with other third-parties.

controls.name: Archived Data Sets
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect archived data in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Information Disposal
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy or erase information.

controls.name: Data Quality Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to check for Redundant, Obsolete/Outdated, Toxic or Trivial (ROTT) data to ensure the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, impact, completeness and de-identification of information throughout the information lifecycle.

controls.name: De-Identification (Anonymization)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to anonymize data by removing Personal Data (PD) from datasets.

controls.name: Information Location
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document the location of information and the specific system components on which the information resides.

controls.name: Transfer of Sensitive and/or Regulated Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict and govern the transfer of sensitive and/or regulated data to third-countries or international organizations.

controls.name: Data Localization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to constrain the impact of "digital sovereignty laws," that require localized data within the host country, where data and processes may be subjected to arbitrary enforcement actions that potentially violate other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Data Rights Management (DRM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Data Rights Management (DRM), or similar technologies, to protect Intellectual Property (IP) rights by preventing the unauthorized distribution and/or modification of sensitive IP.

controls.name: Embedded Technology Security Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of embedded technology controls.

controls.name: Internet of Things (IOT)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively manage the security, compliance and resilience risks associated with Internet of Things (IoT).

controls.name: Operational Technology (OT)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively manage the security, compliance and resilience risks associated with Operational Technology (OT).

controls.name: Interface Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect embedded devices against unauthorized use of the physical factory diagnostic and test interface(s).

controls.name: Embedded Technology Configuration Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to generate log entries on embedded devices when configuration changes or attempts to access interfaces are detected.

controls.name: Prevent Alterations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect embedded devices by preventing the unauthorized installation and execution of software.

controls.name: Embedded Technology Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely update software and upgrade functionality on embedded devices.

controls.name: Resilience To Outages
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure embedded technology to be resilient to data network and power outages.

controls.name: Power Level Monitoring
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to monitor the power levels of embedded technologies for decreased or excessive power usage, including battery drainage, to investigate for device tampering.

controls.name: Embedded Technology Reviews
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform evaluations of deployed embedded technologies as needed, or at least on an annual basis, to ensure that necessary updates to mitigate the risks associated with legacy embedded technologies are identified and implemented.

controls.name: Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce the security of Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) traffic.

controls.name: Restrict Communications
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require embedded technologies to initiate all communications and drop new, incoming communications.

controls.name: Authorized Communications
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict embedded technologies to communicate only with authorized peers and service endpoints.

controls.name: Operating Environment Certification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to determine if embedded technologies are certified for secure use in the proposed operating environment.

controls.name: Safety Assessment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to evaluate the safety aspects of embedded technologies via a fault tree analysis, or similar method, to determine possible consequences of misuse, misconfiguration and/or failure.

controls.name: Certificate-Based Authentication
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce certificate-based authentication for embedded technologies (e.g., IoT, OT, etc.) and their supporting services.

controls.name: Chip-To-Cloud Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement embedded technologies that utilize pre-provisioned cloud trust anchors to support secure bootstrap and Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP).

controls.name: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure embedded technologies utilize a securely configured Real-Time Operating System (RTOS).

controls.name: Safe Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to continuously validate autonomous systems that trigger an automatic state change when safe operation is no longer assured.

controls.name: Endpoint Device Management (EDM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of Endpoint Device Management (EDM) controls.

controls.name: Endpoint Protection Measures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety of endpoint devices.

controls.name: Prohibit Installation Without Privileged Status
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to prohibit software installations without explicitly assigned privileged status.

controls.name: Malicious Code Protection (Anti-Malware)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize antimalware technologies to detect and eradicate malicious code.

controls.name: Software Firewall
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize host-based firewall software, or a similar technology, on all endpoint devices, where technically feasible.

controls.name: Endpoint File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar technologies, to detect and report on unauthorized changes to selected files and configuration settings.

controls.name: Host Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Host-based Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS), or similar technologies, to monitor for and protect against anomalous host activity, including lateral movement across the network.

controls.name: Phishing & Spam Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize anti-phishing and spam protection technologies to detect and take action on unsolicited messages transported by electronic mail.

controls.name: Trusted Path
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish a trusted communications path between the user and the security functions of the operating system.

controls.name: Mobile Code
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address mobile code / operating system-independent applications.

controls.name: Thin Nodes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure thin nodes to have minimal functionality and information storage.

controls.name: Port & Input / Output (I/O) Device Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to physically disable or remove unnecessary connection ports or input/output devices from sensitive systems.

controls.name: Sensor Capability
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to configure embedded sensors on systems to: 
(1) Prohibit the remote activation of sensing capabilities; and
(2) Provide an explicit indication of sensor use to users.

controls.name: Collaborative Computing Devices
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to unplug or prohibit the remote activation of collaborative computing devices with the following exceptions: 
(1) Networked whiteboards; 
(2) Video teleconference cameras; and 
(3) Teleconference microphones.

controls.name: Hypervisor Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict access to hypervisor management functions or administrative consoles for systems hosting virtualized systems.

controls.name: Restrict Access To Security Functions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure security functions are restricted to authorized individuals and enforce least privilege control requirements for necessary job functions.

controls.name: Human Resources Security Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of personnel security controls.

controls.name: Position Categorization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage personnel security risk by assigning a risk designation to all positions and establishing screening criteria for individuals filling those positions.

controls.name: Defined Roles & Responsibilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define cybersecurity roles & responsibilities for all personnel.

controls.name: Personnel Screening
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage personnel security risk by screening individuals prior to authorizing access.

controls.name: Terms of Employment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require all employees and contractors to apply cybersecurity and data protection principles in their daily work to enable secure, compliant and resilient capabilities.

controls.name: Access Agreements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require internal and third-party users to sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access.

controls.name: Personnel Sanctions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to sanction personnel failing to comply with established security policies, standards and procedures.

controls.name: Personnel Transfer
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to adjust logical and physical access authorizations to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and facilities upon personnel reassignment or transfer, in a timely manner.

controls.name: Personnel Termination
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern the termination of individual employment.

controls.name: Third-Party Personnel
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern third-party personnel by reviewing and monitoring third-party security, compliance and/or resilience roles and responsibilities.

controls.name: Separation of Duties (SoD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and maintain Separation of Duties (SoD) to prevent potential inappropriate activity without collusion.

controls.name: Incompatible Roles
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to avoid incompatible development-specific roles through limiting and reviewing developer privileges to change hardware, software and firmware components within a production/operational environment.

controls.name: Identify Critical Skills & Gaps
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to evaluate the critical security, compliance and resilience skills needed to support the organization's mission and identify gaps that exist.

controls.name: Identifying Authorized Work Locations
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to identify and document authorized working locations, including:
(1) Designated on-premises, organization-controlled work locations; and
(2) Other off-premises locations not under organization-control (e.g., work from home).

controls.name: Reporting Suspicious Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enable personnel to report suspicious activities and/or behavior without fear of reprisal or other negative consequences (e.g., whistleblower protections).

controls.name: Identity & Access Management (IAM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of identification and access management controls.

controls.name: Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) organizational users and processes acting on behalf of organizational users.

controls.name: Identification & Authentication for Non-Organizational Users
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) third-party users and processes that provide services to the organization.

controls.name: Identification & Authentication for Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) devices before establishing a connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically- based and replay resistant.

controls.name: Identification & Authentication for Third-Party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and authenticate third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
controls.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
(1) Remote network access; 
(2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
(3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive/regulated data.

controls.name: User Provisioning & De-Provisioning
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a formal user registration and de-registration process that governs the assignment of access rights.

controls.name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to restrict access to individuals assigned specific roles with legitimate business needs.

controls.name: Identifier Management (User Names)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to govern naming standards for usernames and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Authenticator Management
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Securely manage authenticators for users and devices; and
(2) Ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the data being accessed.

controls.name: Authenticator Feedback
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to obscure the feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation/use by unauthorized individuals.

controls.name: Cryptographic Module Authentication
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure cryptographic modules adhere to applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements for security strength.

controls.name: Adaptive Identification & Authentication
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allow individuals to utilize alternative methods of authentication under specific circumstances or situations.

controls.name: Re-Authentication
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to force users and devices to re-authenticate according to organization-defined circumstances that necessitate re-authentication.

controls.name: Account Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively govern account management of individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts.

controls.name: Privileged Account Management (PAM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict and control privileged access rights for users and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Periodic Review of Account Privileges
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically-review the privileges assigned to individuals and service accounts to validate the need for such privileges and reassign or remove unnecessary privileges, as necessary.

controls.name: User Responsibilities for Account Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to compel users to follow accepted practices in the use of authentication mechanisms (e.g., passwords, passphrases, physical or logical security tokens, smart cards, certificates, etc.).

controls.name: Credential Sharing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent the sharing of generic IDs, passwords or other generic authentication methods.

controls.name: Access Enforcement
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."

controls.name: Least Privilege
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize the concept of least privilege, allowing only authorized access to processes necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational business functions.

controls.name: Account Lockout
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce a limit for consecutive invalid login attempts by a user during an organization-defined time period and automatically locks the account when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

controls.name: Concurrent Session Control
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit the number of concurrent sessions for each system account.

controls.name: Session Lock
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to initiate a session lock after an organization-defined time period of inactivity, or upon receiving a request from a user and retain the session lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication methods.

controls.name: Session Termination
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to log out users, both locally on the network and for remote sessions, at the end of the session or after an organization-defined period of inactivity.

controls.name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authorization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document the supporting rationale for specific user actions that can be performed on a system without identification or authentication.

controls.name: Reference Monitor
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement a reference monitor that is tamperproof, always-invoked, small enough to be subject to analysis / testing and the completeness of which can be assured.

controls.name: Identity Proofing (Identity Verification)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to verify the identity of a user before issuing authenticators or modifying access permissions.

controls.name: Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) for policy-driven, dynamic authorizations that supports the secure sharing of information.

controls.name: Mutual Authentication (MA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Mutual Authentication (MA) where both sides of a communications channel verify the identity of the other party through certificate exchange.

controls.name: Incident Response Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern processes and documentation to facilitate an organization-wide response capability for cybersecurity and data protection-related incidents.

controls.name: Incident Handling
Indicators of Compromise (IOC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define specific Indicators of Compromise (IOC) to identify the signs of potential cybersecurity events.

controls.name: Incident Response Plan (IRP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain and make available a current and viable Incident Response Plan (IRP) to all stakeholders.

controls.name: Incident Response Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to train personnel in their incident response roles and responsibilities.

controls.name: Incident Response Testing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to formally test incident response capabilities through realistic exercises to determine the operational effectiveness of those capabilities.

controls.name: Integrated Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish an integrated team of cybersecurity, IT and business function representatives that are capable of addressing cybersecurity and data protection incident response operations.

controls.name: Chain of Custody & Forensics
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform digital forensics and maintain the integrity of the chain of custody, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and industry-recognized secure practices.

controls.name: Situational Awareness For Incidents
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to document, monitor and report the status of cybersecurity and data protection incidents to internal stakeholders all the way through the resolution of the incident.

controls.name: Incident Stakeholder Reporting
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to timely-report incidents to applicable:
(1) Internal stakeholders; 
(2) Affected clients & third-parties; and
(3) Regulatory authorities.

controls.name: Incident Reporting Assistance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide incident response advice and assistance to users of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for the handling and reporting of actual and potential cybersecurity and data protection incidents.

controls.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Response
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to respond to sensitive/regulated data spills.

controls.name: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to incorporate lessons learned from analyzing and resolving cybersecurity and data protection incidents to reduce the likelihood or impact of future incidents.

controls.name: Regulatory & Law Enforcement Contacts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain incident response contacts with applicable regulatory and law enforcement agencies.

controls.name: Detonation Chambers (Sandboxes)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a detonation chamber capability to detect and/or block potentially-malicious files and email attachments.

controls.name: Public Relations & Reputation Repair
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively manage public relations associated with incidents and employ appropriate measures to prevent further reputational damage and develop plans to repair any damage to the organization's reputation.

controls.name: Information Assurance (IA) Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of security, compliance and resilience assessment and authorization controls.

controls.name: Assessments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to formally assess the security, compliance and resilience controls in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting expected requirements.

controls.name: Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to generate authoritative documentation (e.g., System Security Plan (SSP)) that:
(1) Identifies key architectural and implementation information on in-scope Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS);
(2) Reflects the current state of applied security, compliance and resilience controls on applicable People, Processes, Technologies, Data and/or Facilities (PPTDF) that are contained within the system boundary; and
(3) Provides a historical record of applied security controls, including changes.

controls.name: Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation During Development
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to create and execute a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to identify and remediate flaws during development.

controls.name: Capabilities Deficiency Tracking
Technical Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to evaluate the design, implementation and effectiveness of technical security, compliance and resilience controls.

controls.name: Security Authorization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are officially authorized prior to "go live" in a production environment.

controls.name: Maintenance Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, disseminate, review & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of maintenance controls across the enterprise.

controls.name: Controlled Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct controlled maintenance activities throughout the lifecycle of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS).

controls.name: Timely Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within a defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO).

controls.name: Maintenance Tools
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control and monitor the use of system maintenance tools.

controls.name: Remote Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to authorize, monitor and control remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic activities.

controls.name: Authorized Maintenance Personnel
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a current list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel.

controls.name: Maintain Configuration Control During Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain proper physical security and configuration control over technology assets awaiting service or repair.

controls.name: Field Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to securely conduct field maintenance on geographically deployed assets.

controls.name: Off-Site Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure off-site maintenance activities are conducted securely and the asset(s) undergoing maintenance actions are secured during physical transfer and storage while off-site.

controls.name: Maintenance Validation
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to validate:
(1) Maintenance activities were appropriately performed according to the work order; and 
(2) Applicable security, compliance and resilience controls are operational.

controls.name: Maintenance Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain situational awareness of the quality and reliability of systems and components through tracking maintenance activities and component failure rates.

controls.name: Centralized Management Of Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern Mobile Device Management (MDM) controls.

controls.name: Access Control For Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce access control requirements for the connection of mobile devices to organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Full Device & Container-Based Encryption
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on mobile devices through full-device or container encryption.

controls.name: Mobile Device Tampering
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect mobile devices from tampering through inspecting devices returning from locations that the organization deems to be of significant risk, prior to the device being connected to the organization's network.

controls.name: Remote Purging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to remotely purge selected information from mobile devices.

controls.name: Personally-Owned Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the connection of personally-owned, mobile devices to organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Organization-Owned Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prohibit the installation of non-approved applications or approved applications not obtained through the organization-approved application store.

controls.name: Mobile Device Data Retention Limitations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit data retention on mobile devices to the smallest usable dataset and timeframe.

controls.name: Mobile Device Geofencing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the functionality of mobile devices based on geographic location.

controls.name: Separate Mobile Device Profiles
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce a separate device workspace on applicable mobile devices to separate work-related and personal-related applications and data.

controls.name: Restricting Access To Authorized Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the connectivity of unauthorized mobile devices from communicating with organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Network Security Controls (NSC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, govern & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of Network Security Controls (NSC).

controls.name: Layered Network Defenses
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security functions as a layered structure that minimizes interactions between layers of the design and avoids any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.

controls.name: Boundary Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor and control communications at the external network boundary and at key internal boundaries within the network.

controls.name: Data Flow Enforcement – Access Control Lists (ACLs)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern Access Control Lists (ACLs) to provide data flow enforcement that explicitly restrict network traffic to only what is authorized.

controls.name: Interconnection Security Agreements (ISAs)
Network Segmentation (macrosegementation)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure network architecture utilizes network segmentation to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to protect from other network resources.

controls.name: Network Connection Termination
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to terminate network connections at the end of a session or after an organization-defined time period of inactivity.

controls.name: Network Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (NIDS / NIPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to employ Network Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (NIDS/NIPS) to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the network.

controls.name: Session Integrity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the authenticity and integrity of communications sessions.

controls.name: Domain Name Service (DNS) Resolution
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Domain Name Service (DNS) resolution is designed, implemented and managed to protect the security of name / address resolution.

controls.name: Out-of-Band Channels
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize out-of-band channels for the electronic transmission of information and/or the physical shipment of system components or devices to authorized individuals.

controls.name: Safeguarding Data Over Open Networks
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to implement strong cryptography and security protocols to safeguard sensitive/regulated data during transmission over open, public networks.

controls.name: Electronic Messaging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic messaging communications.

controls.name: Remote Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define, control and review organization-approved, secure remote access methods.

controls.name: Wireless Networking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control authorized wireless usage and monitor for unauthorized wireless access.

controls.name: Intranets
controls.description:
