Mechanisms exist to establish trust relationships with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining intranet systems, allowing authorized individuals to: 
(1) Access the intranet from external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and
(2) Process, store, and/or transmit organization-controlled information using the external TAAS.

controls.name: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to protect sensitive information as it is stored, transmitted and processed.

controls.name: DNS & Content Filtering
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to force Internet-bound network traffic through a proxy device (e.g., Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)) for URL content filtering and DNS filtering to limit a user's ability to connect to dangerous or prohibited Internet sites.

controls.name: Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR)
controls.description: Automated Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR) mechanisms exist to detect the presence of unapproved active content and facilitate its removal, resulting in content with only known safe elements.

controls.name: Email Content Protections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement an email filtering security service to detect malicious attachments in emails and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.name: Physical & Environmental Protections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the operation of physical and environmental protection controls.

controls.name: Physical Access Authorizations
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to maintain a current list of personnel with authorized access to organizational facilities (except for those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).

controls.name: Physical Access Control
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to enforce physical access authorizations for all physical access points (including designated entry/exit points) to facilities (excluding those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).

controls.name: Physical Security of Offices, Rooms & Facilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify systems, equipment and respective operating environments that require limited physical access so that appropriate physical access controls are designed and implemented for offices, rooms and facilities.

controls.name: Monitoring Physical Access
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor for, detect and respond to physical security incidents.

controls.name: Visitor Control
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to identify, authorize and monitor visitors before allowing access to the facility (other than areas designated as publicly accessible).

controls.name: Supporting Utilities
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.

controls.name: Fire Protection
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize and maintain fire suppression and detection devices/systems for the system that are supported by an independent energy source.

controls.name: Temperature & Humidity Controls
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to maintain and monitor temperature and humidity levels within the facility.

controls.name: Delivery & Removal
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to isolate information processing facilities from points such as delivery and loading areas and other points to avoid unauthorized access.

controls.name: Alternate Work Site
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to utilize appropriate management, operational and technical controls at alternate work sites.

controls.name: Equipment Siting & Protection
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to locate system components within the facility to minimize potential damage from physical and environmental hazards and to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.

controls.name: Information Leakage Due To Electromagnetic Signals Emanations
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect the system from information leakage due to electromagnetic signals emanations.

controls.name: Asset Monitoring and Tracking
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to employ asset location technologies that track and monitor the location and movement of organization-defined assets within organization-defined controlled areas.

controls.name: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Protection
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to employ safeguards against Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) damage for systems and system components.

controls.name: Component Marking
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to mark system hardware components indicating the impact or classification level of the information permitted to be processed, stored or transmitted by the hardware component.

controls.name: Proximity Sensor
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to monitor physical proximity to robotic or autonomous platforms to reduce applied force or stop the operation when sensors indicate a potentially dangerous scenario.

controls.name: On-Site Client Segregation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure client-specific sensitive/regulated data is isolated from other data when client-specific sensitive/regulated data is processed or stored within multi-client workspaces.

controls.name: Physical Access Device Inventories
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain an accurate inventory of all physical access devices (e.g., RFID cards, access fobs, door keys, etc.).

controls.name: Data Privacy Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and operation of data protection controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure all forms of Personal Data (PD) are processed lawfully, fairly and transparently.

controls.name: Data Privacy Notice
Choice & Consent
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to enable data subjects to authorize the collection, receiving, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, updating and/or disposal of their Personal Data (PD), where prior to collection the data subject is provided with:
(1) Plain language to illustrate the potential data privacy risks of the authorization; 
(2) A means for users to decline the authorization; and
(3) All necessary choice and consent-related criteria required by applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.name: Restrict Collection To Identified Purpose
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize the collection of Personal Data (PD) to only what is adequate, relevant and limited to the purposes identified in the data privacy notice, including protections against collecting PD from minors without appropriate parental or legal guardian consent.

controls.name: Personal Data (PD) Retention & Disposal
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to: 
(1) Retain Personal Data (PD), including metadata, for an organization-defined time period to fulfill the purpose(s) identified in the notice or as required by law;
(2) Dispose of, destroys, erases, and/or anonymizes the PD, regardless of the method of storage; and
(3) Use organization-defined techniques or methods to ensure secure deletion or destruction of PD (including originals, copies and archived records).

controls.name: Data Subject Empowerment
Information Sharing With Third Parties
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to disclose Personal Data (PD) to third-parties only for the purposes identified in the data privacy notice and with the implicit or explicit consent of the data subject.

controls.name: Personal Data (PD) Control Testing, Training & Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct testing, training and monitoring activities for Personal Data (PD) controls.

controls.name: Personal Data (PD) Lineage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a process to document the lineage of Personal Data (PD) by recording how the organization collects, receives, processes, stores, transmits, shares, updates and/or disposes PD.

controls.name: Data Quality Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage the quality, utility, objectivity, integrity and impact determination and de-identification of sensitive/regulated data across the information lifecycle.

controls.name: Data Tagging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to issue data modeling guidelines to support tagging of sensitive/regulated data.

controls.name: Updating Personal Data (PD) Process
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to identify and record:
(1) The process(es) used to update Personal Data (PD); and
(2) The frequency that such updates occur.

controls.name: Data Management Board
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish a written charter for a Data Management Board (DMB) and assigned organization-defined roles to the DMB.

controls.name: Documenting Data Processing Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to document Personal Data (PD) processing activities that covers collection, receiving, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, updating and/or disposal actions with sufficient detail to demonstrate conformity with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.

controls.name: Register As A Data Controller and/or Data Processor
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to register as a data controller and/or data processor, including registering databases containing Personal Data (PD) with the appropriate Data Authority, when necessary.

controls.name: Potential Human Rights Abuses
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to constrain the supply of physical and/or digital activity logs to the host government that can directly lead to contravention of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), as well as other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Data Subject Communications
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to craft disclosures and communications to data subjects in a manner that is concise, unambiguous and understandable by a reasonable person.

controls.name: Data Controller Communications
Automated Decision-Making Technology (ADMT) For Data Subject Actions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure data subject actions utilizing Automated Decision-Making Technology (ADMT) where computation replaces, or substantially replaces, human decisionmaking, conforms with all applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Data Brokers
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure data brokers that collect Personal Data (PD) from a source other than directly from the data subject adhere to all applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations.

controls.name: Notice of Right To Opt-Out
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to include a notification to data subjects within the data privacy notice of:
(1) Their right to direct an organization that sells or shares their Personal Data (PD) to stop selling or sharing their PD; and
(2) The methods available to exercise that right.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Protection Portfolio Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of resource planning controls that provide a portfolio management approach to achieve security, compliance and resilience objectives.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Resource Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address all capital planning and investment requests, including the resources needed to implement the Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) and document all exceptions to this requirement.

controls.name: Allocation of Resources
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and allocate resources for management, operational, technical and data protection requirements within business process planning for projects / initiatives.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience In Project Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to assess security, compliance and resilience controls in system project development to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the requirements.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) at pre-defined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

controls.name: Business Process Definition
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to define business processes with consideration for security, compliance and resilience that determines: 
(1) The resulting risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals and other organizations; and
(2) Information protection needs arising from the defined business processes and revises the processes as necessary, until an achievable set of protection needs is obtained.

controls.name: Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC) Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure changes to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC) are controlled through formal change control procedures.

controls.name: Manage Organizational Knowledge
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage the organizational knowledge of the security, compliance and resilience staff.

controls.name: Risk Management Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls.

controls.name: Risk-Based Security Categorization
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to categorize Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations that:
(1) Document the security categorization results (including supporting rationale) in the security plan for systems; and
(2) Ensure the security categorization decision is reviewed and approved by the asset owner.

controls.name: Risk Identification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document risks, both internal and external.

controls.name: Risk Assessment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct recurring assessments of risk that includes the likelihood and magnitude of harm, from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.name: Risk Ranking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and assign a risk ranking to newly discovered security vulnerabilities that is based on industry-recognized practices.

controls.name: Risk Remediation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to remediate risks to an acceptable level.

controls.name: Risk Assessment Update
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to routinely update risk assessments and react accordingly upon identifying new security vulnerabilities, including using outside sources for security vulnerability information.

controls.name: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) to identify and assess security, compliance and resilience risks.

controls.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a plan for Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance and disposal of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including documenting selected mitigating actions and monitoring performance against those plans.

controls.name: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) on Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that store, process and/or transmit Personal Data (PD) to identify and remediate reasonably-expected risks.

controls.name: Risk Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure risk monitoring as an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy that includes monitoring the effectiveness of security, compliance and resilience controls, compliance and change management.

controls.name: Risk Culture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates technology-related risk.

controls.name: Executive Leadership Approval For Managing Material Risk
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to obtain executive leadership approval for risk management decisions involving material risk.

controls.name: Secure Engineering Principles
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of industry-recognized security, compliance and resilience practices in the specification, design, development, implementation and modification of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Alignment With Enterprise Architecture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop an enterprise architecture, aligned with industry-recognized leading practices, with consideration for security, compliance and resilience principles that addresses risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals and other organizations.

controls.name: Defense-In-Depth (DiD) Architecture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.

controls.name: Process Isolation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement a separate execution domain for each executing process.

controls.name: Information In Shared Resources
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.

controls.name: Prevent Program Execution
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to prevent the execution of unauthorized software programs.

controls.name: Predictable Failure Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to determine the Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) for system components in specific environments of operation.

controls.name: Non-Persistence
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement non-persistent system components and services that are initiated in a known state and terminated upon the end of the session of use or periodically at an organization-defined frequency.

controls.name: Information Output Filtering
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to validate information output from software programs and/or applications to ensure that the information is consistent with the expected content.

controls.name: Memory Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security safeguards to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution.

controls.name: Honeypots
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize honeypots that are specifically designed to be the target of malicious attacks for the purpose of detecting, deflecting and analyzing such attacks.

controls.name: Honeyclients
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize honeyclients that proactively seek to identify malicious websites and/or web-based malicious code.

controls.name: Heterogeneity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a diverse set of technologies for system components to reduce the impact of technical vulnerabilities from the same Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).

controls.name: Concealment & Misdirection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize concealment and misdirection techniques for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to confuse and mislead adversaries.

controls.name: Distributed Processing & Storage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to distribute processing and storage across multiple physical locations.

controls.name: Non-Modifiable Executable Programs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize non-modifiable executable programs that load and execute the operating environment and applications from hardware-enforced, read-only media.

controls.name: Secure Log-On Procedures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a trusted communications path between the user and the security functions of the system.

controls.name: System Use Notification (Logon Banner)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize system use notification / logon banners that display an approved system use notification message or banner before granting access to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Previous Logon Notification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure systems that process, store or transmit sensitive/regulated data to notify the user, upon successful logon, of the number of unsuccessful logon attempts since the last successful logon.

controls.name: Clock Synchronization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize time-synchronization technology to synchronize all critical system clocks.

controls.name: Application Container
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize an application container (virtualization approach) to isolate to a known set of dependencies, access methods and interfaces.

controls.name: Privileged Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent privileged operating environments from existing within unprivileged operating environments, including physical or virtual deployments of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Operations Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of operational security controls.

controls.name: Security Concept Of Operations (CONOPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a security Concept of Operations (CONOPS), or a similarly-defined plan for achieving cybersecurity objectives, that documents management, operational and technical measures implemented to apply defense-in-depth techniques that is communicated to all appropriate stakeholders.

controls.name:
Service Delivery
(Business Process Support)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define supporting business processes and implement appropriate governance and service management to ensure appropriate planning, delivery and support of the organization's technology capabilities supporting business functions, workforce, and/or customers based on industry-recognized standards to achieve the specific goals of the process area.

controls.name: Security Operations Center (SOC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish and maintain a Security Operations Center (SOC) that facilitates a 24x7 response capability.

controls.name: Secure Practices Guidelines
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide guidelines and recommendations for the secure use of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to assist in the configuration, installation and use of the product and/or service.

controls.name: Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) tools to define, prioritize and automate the response to security incidents.

controls.name: Shadow Information Technology Detection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to detect the presence of unauthorized Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in use.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience-Minded Workforce
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of security workforce development and awareness controls.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Awareness Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide all employees and contractors appropriate security, compliance and resilience awareness education and training that is relevant for their job function.

controls.name: Role-Based Security, Compliance & Resilience Training
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide role-based security, compliance and resilience-related training: 
(1) Before authorizing access to the system or performing assigned duties; 
(2) When required by system changes; and 
(3) Annually thereafter.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Training Records
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to document, retain and monitor individual training activities, including:
(1) Initial security, compliance and resilience awareness training;
(2) Recurring awareness training; and
(3) Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)-specific training.

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Knowledge Sharing
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to improve knowledge sharing across security, compliance and resilience personnel allowing for:
(1) Efficient operations; and
(2) Rapid and effective response to incidents.

controls.name: Technology Development & Acquisition
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of tailored development and acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods to meet unique business needs.

controls.name: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Security Requirements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to design, develop and produce Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in such a way that risk-based technical and functional specifications ensure Minimum Viable Product (MVP) criteria establish an appropriate level of security and resiliency based on applicable risks and threats.

controls.name: Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Security Solutions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize only Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) security products.

controls.name: Documentation Requirements
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to obtain, protect and distribute administrator documentation for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that describe:
(1) Secure configuration, installation and operation of the TAAS;
(2) Effective use and maintenance of security features/functions; and
(3) Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (e.g., privileged) functions.

controls.name: Developer Architecture & Design
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce a design specification and security architecture that: 
(1) Is consistent with and supportive of the organization's security architecture which is established within and is an integrated part of the organization's enterprise architecture;
(2) Accurately and completely describes the required security functionality and the allocation of security, compliance and resilience controls among physical and logical components; and
(3) Expresses how individual security functions, mechanisms and services work together to provide required security capabilities and a unified approach to protection.

controls.name: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop applications based on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP).

controls.name: Secure Development Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a segmented development network to ensure a secure development environment.

controls.name: Separation of Development, Testing and Operational Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage separate development, testing and operational environments to reduce the risks of unauthorized access or changes to the operational environment and to ensure no impact to production Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Testing Throughout Development
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to require system developers/integrators consult with security, compliance and/or resilience personnel to: 
(1) Create and implement a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar capability;
(2) Implement a verifiable flaw remediation process to correct weaknesses and deficiencies identified during the control testing and evaluation process; and
(3) Document the results.

controls.name: Use of Live Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to approve, document and control the use of live data in development and test environments.

controls.name: Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain awareness of component authenticity by developing and implementing Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC) practices that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components.

controls.name: Customized Development of Critical Components
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to custom-develop critical system components, when Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) solutions are unavailable.

controls.name: Developer Screening
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) have the requisite skillset and appropriate access authorizations.

controls.name: Developer Configuration Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to perform configuration management during system design, development, implementation and operation.

controls.name: Developer Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to develop and implement an ongoing Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to objectively identify and remediate vulnerabilities prior to release to production.

controls.name: Developer-Provided Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to provide training on the correct use and operation of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS).

controls.name: Unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to prevent unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by:
(1) Removing and/or replacing TAAS when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor or manufacturer; and
(2) Requiring justification and documented approval for the continued use of unsupported TAAS required to satisfy mission/business needs.

controls.name: Input Data Validation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to check the validity of information inputs.

controls.name: Error Handling
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to handle error conditions by: 
(1) Identifying potentially security-relevant error conditions;
(2) Generating error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing sensitive or potentially harmful information in error logs and administrative messages that could be exploited; and
(3) Revealing error messages only to authorized personnel.

controls.name: Access to Program Source Code
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit privileges to change software resident within software libraries.

controls.name: Product Conformity Governance
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to ensure developed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) conform to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, based on the product's and/or service's:
(1) Use case(s); and
(2) Geographic markets.

controls.name: Technical Documentation Artifacts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to generate appropriate technical documentation artifacts for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in sufficient detail to demonstrate conformity with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual compliance requirements.

controls.name: Third-Party Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of third-party management controls.

controls.name: Third-Party Criticality Assessments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify, prioritize and assess suppliers and partners of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) using a supply chain risk assessment process relative to their importance in supporting the delivery of high-value services.

controls.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Evaluate security risks and threats associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) supply chains; and
(2) Take appropriate remediation actions to minimize the organization's exposure to those risks and threats, as necessary.

controls.name: Third-Party Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to mitigate the risks associated with third-party access to the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.name: Third-Party Personnel Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control personnel security requirements including security roles and responsibilities for third-party providers.

controls.name: Monitoring for Third-Party Information Disclosure
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of organizational information.

controls.name: Review of Third-Party Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor, regularly review and assess External Service Providers (ESPs) for compliance with established contractual requirements for security, compliance and resilience controls.

controls.name: Third-Party Deficiency Remediation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address weaknesses or deficiencies in supply chain elements identified during independent or organizational assessments of such elements.

controls.name: Managing Changes To Third-Party Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control changes to services by suppliers, taking into account the criticality of business Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that are in scope by the third-party.

controls.name: Third-Party Incident Response & Recovery Capabilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure response/recovery planning and testing are conducted with critical suppliers/providers.

controls.name: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices.

controls.name: Threat Intelligence Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement a threat intelligence program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability that can influence the development of the system and security architectures, selection of security solutions, monitoring, threat hunting, response and recovery activities.

controls.name: Indicators of Exposure (IOE)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop Indicators of Exposure (IOE) to understand the potential attack vectors that attackers could use to attack the organization.

controls.name: Threat Intelligence Feeds
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain situational awareness of vulnerabilities and evolving threats by leveraging the knowledge of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures to facilitate the implementation of preventative and compensating controls.

controls.name: Insider Threat Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement an insider threat program that includes a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team.

controls.name: Insider Threat Awareness
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.

controls.name: Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish a Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) to assist with the secure development and maintenance of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that receives unsolicited input from the public about vulnerabilities in organizational TAAS.

controls.name: Threat Hunting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform cyber threat hunting that uses Indicators of Compromise (IoC) to detect, track and disrupt threats that evade existing security controls.

controls.name: Tainting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to embed false data or steganographic data in files to enable the organization to determine if data has been exfiltrated and provide a means to identify the individual(s) involved.

controls.name: Threat Catalog
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop and keep current a catalog of applicable internal and external threats to the organization, both natural and manmade.

controls.name: Threat Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify, assess, prioritize and document the potential impact(s) and likelihood(s) of applicable internal and external threats.

controls.name: Behavioral Baselining
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to establish behavioral baselines that capture information about user and entity behavior to enable dynamic threat discovery.

controls.name: Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and monitoring of vulnerability management controls.

controls.name: Vulnerability Remediation Process
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that vulnerabilities are properly identified, tracked and remediated.

controls.name: Vulnerability Ranking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and assign a risk ranking to newly discovered security vulnerabilities using reputable outside sources for security vulnerability information.

controls.name: Continuous Vulnerability Remediation Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address new threats and vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis and ensure assets are protected against known attacks.

controls.name: Software & Firmware Patching
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct software patching for all deployed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including firmware.

controls.name: Vulnerability Scanning
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to detect vulnerabilities and configuration errors by routine vulnerability scanning of systems and applications.

controls.name: Penetration Testing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct penetration testing on Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.name: Technical Surveillance Countermeasures Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a technical surveillance countermeasures survey.

controls.name: Reviewing Vulnerability Scanner Usage
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor logs associated with scanning activities and associated administrator accounts to ensure that those activities are limited to the timeframes of legitimate scans.

controls.name: Red Team Exercises
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize "red team" exercises to simulate attempts by adversaries to compromise Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in accordance with organization-defined rules of engagement.

controls.name: Web Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of an enterprise-wide web management policy, as well as associated standards, controls and procedures.

controls.name: Use of Demilitarized Zones (DMZ)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) to restrict inbound traffic to authorized Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) on certain services, protocols and ports.

controls.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to deploy Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) to provide defense-in-depth protection for application-specific threats.

controls.name: Client-Facing Web Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to deploy reasonably-expected security, compliance and resilience controls to protect the confidentiality and availability of client data that is stored, transmitted or processed by the Internet-based service.

controls.name: Cookie Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide individuals with clear and precise information about cookies, in accordance with applicable legal requirements for cookie management.

controls.name: Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) for consumers to reasonably prove their identity.

controls.name: Web Security Standard
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Application Security Verification Standard is incorporated into the organization's Secure Systems Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) process.

controls.name: Web Application Framework
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure a robust Web Application Framework is used to aid in the development of secure web applications, including web services, web resources and web APIs.

controls.name: Validation & Sanitization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure all input handled by a web application is validated and/or sanitized.

controls.name: Secure Web Traffic
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure all web application content is delivered using cryptographic mechanisms (e.g., TLS).

controls.name: Output Encoding
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure output encoding is performed on all content produced by a web application to reduce the likelihood of cross-site scripting and other injection attacks.

controls.name: Web Browser Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure web applications implement Content-Security-Policy, HSTS and X-Frame-Options response headers to protect both the web application and its users.

controls.name: Website Change Detection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to detect and respond to Indicators of Compromise (IoC) for unauthorized alterations, additions, deletions or changes on websites that store, process and/or transmit sensitive/regulated data.

controls.name: Publicly Accessible Content Reviews
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to routinely review the content on publicly accessible systems for sensitive/regulated data and remove such information, if discovered.
